text:
Charle-Edouard D'Astous went undrafted, spent his mid-twenties in Sweden and arrived in Tampa Bay last season at 27. Now, as CBS Sports put it, he's powering toward career highs: 14 points in 23 games after 29 in 70 last season, with half of them on the power play and his ice time up to almost 19 minutes over his last ten.

The Lightning play well with him out there. They take about 58% of expected goals at five on five on his shifts, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the 86th percentile of defensemen for driving play last season, so this isn't purely a hot streak.

Some of the scoring is, though. He has four goals on 2.4 expected, shooting about 12% when a typical defenseman shoots around 6%, and his teammates have scored nearly five goals more than their chances while he's on the ice. Our range puts him nearer 41 points by season's end than the pace he's on now. What to watch: whether he keeps the power-play role as the bounces settle.
headline: D'Astous is no longer a surprise
